name: Anisotropic Covariance
definition: Allows 3D Gaussians to scale anisotropically along the x, y, and z axes and rotate in 3D space, rather than remaining spherical, to better fit scene geometry.
summary: Anisotropic Covariance enables 3D Gaussian primitives to scale and rotate along distinct axes, replacing spherical shapes to accurately model elongated structures and avoid the blurring artifacts of isotropic methods.
